name: MathlibAnnex.PluckerSupport.pluckerPairing_satelliteCoefficients_maximalMinors
title: The satellite polynomial is linear in the maximal-minor vector

content.display_title: The satellite polynomial is linear in the maximal-minor vector
content.one_sentence_role: Expresses the configuration polynomial as a linear pairing with maximal minors.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n=m+1>0$ and let $J$ be finite, possibly empty. On $V=\mathbb R^n$ fix real linear functionals $F=(\ell_i)_{i=1}^n$ and $s=(s_a)_{a\in J}$. Put $M_F=(\ell_i(e_j))_{i,j}$ in the standard basis, and let $M_F[i\leftarrow s_a]$ replace row $i$ by $(s_a(e_j))_j$. Set
$$A_{(F,s)}x=((\ell_i(x))_i,(s_a(x))_a)\in\mathbb R^{n+|J|}.$$
Enumerate $J$ to place its rows after the base rows. For a real linear map $A:V\to\mathbb R^{n+|J|}$, let $A_{ij}=(Ae_j)_i$. For each increasing $n$-row index $I$, put $\Pi_n(A)_I=\det(A_{I,*})$. Let $I_0$ select all base rows and $I_{i,a}$ select all base rows except $i$, followed by satellite $a$. Let $e_I$ denote a minor-coordinate unit vector. Given any $w\in\mathbb R$ and coefficients $c_a\in V$, put
$$\Omega_{w,c}=we_{I_0}+\sum_{a\in J}\sum_{i=1}^n(c_a)_i(-1)^{n-i} e_{I_{i,a}},$$
$$\Phi_{w,c}(F,s)=w\det M_F+\sum_{a\in J}\sum_{i=1}^n(c_a)_i\det M_F[i\leftarrow s_a].$$
Then the finite dot product satisfies
$$\langle\Omega_{w,c},\Pi_n(A_{(F,s)})\rangle=\Phi_{w,c}(F,s).$$
content.assumptions: The finite families, arbitrary real weight and coefficients are the only inputs. No norm model, admissibility or maximizing condition is assumed.
content.conclusion: The same configuration appears in the map and polynomial. The parity corrects increasing-row order to row-replacement order.
content.proof_summary: Read the row sign, expand both finite sums, and substitute their determinant identities.

proof_steps.text:
**Correct the selected row order.** Moving the last selected satellite row into position $i$ crosses $n-i$ rows. Therefore
$$(-1)^{n-i}\Pi_n(A_{(F,s)})_{I_{i,a}}=\det M_F[i\leftarrow s_a],\qquad
\Pi_n(A_{(F,s)})_{I_0}=\det M_F.$$
The [inverse cycle in the source](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Operator/PluckerSupport.lean#L225-L227) maps position $i$ to the last selected row. [the parity-corrected minor lemma](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Operator/PluckerSupport.lean#L292-L303) applies to this same configuration, $i$ and $a$. In zero-based source indexing $i_0=i-1$, the parity is $(-1)^{m-i_0}=(-1)^{n-i}$. The pinned [row-permutation determinant formula](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/360da6fa66c1273b76b6b2d8c5666fd5ac2e3b56/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Determinant/Basic.lean#L213-L215) says $\det(M_{\sigma,*})=\operatorname{sign}(\sigma)\det M$; substitute the inverse cycle that moves the last selected row to $i$.

**Show both sums in the pairing.** Bilinearity gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\langle\Omega_{w,c},\Pi_n(A_{(F,s)})\rangle
&=w\Pi_n(A_{(F,s)})_{I_0}\\
&\quad+\sum_{a\in J}\sum_{i=1}^n(c_a)_i(-1)^{n-i}
 \Pi_n(A_{(F,s)})_{I_{i,a}}\\
&=w\det M_F+\sum_{a\in J}\sum_{i=1}^n(c_a)_i\det M_F[i\leftarrow s_a]\\
&=\Phi_{w,c}(F,s).
\end{aligned}$$
The first equality expands [the coefficient vector RHS](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Operator/PluckerSupport.lean#L305-L311); the second substitutes Step 1. If $J$ is empty the sums vanish and the identity reduces to $w\det M_F$.

content.lean_realization_notes:
The [product-indexed map](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Operator/FiniteSup.lean#L372-L375) and [finite-coordinate map](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Operator/FiniteSup.lean#L464-L467) both send $x$ to its base and satellite evaluations, as in the displayed definition of $A_{(F,s)}$. Extracting the rows of a linear map and reassembling them gives that same map, by [the reconstruction identity](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Operator/FiniteSup.lean#L529-L542).

For the later volume-scaled application, let $p$ be a norm, $K_p=\{x:p(x)\le1\}$ and $v_p=\lambda(K_p)$ its reference Lebesgue volume. The [volume-scaling identity](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/VolumeScaledMaximalMinor.lean#L29-L38) gives
$$\langle\Omega_{w,c},v_p\Pi_n(A_{(F,s)})\rangle=v_p\Phi_{w,c}(F,s).$$
Neither the norm nor the volume factor is an input to the unscaled theorem above.
